evidence: Core behaviour is graded heavily and server-backed state is proven with independent contexts, re-auth and a real process restart. (1) Defining behaviour: functional/judge.toml grades one-stage moves (hro_move_one_stage w1.5), interview places (hro_interview_full w1.5), stale-move refusal naming the actor (hro_stale_refused w2.5), all-or-none bulk moves (hro_bulk_all_or_none w2), undo/undo conflict (hro_undo_restores, hro_undo_conflict w2), live board within 15 s (hro_live_board w2.5), message exchange, unread/seen, paging, candidate privacy. (2) Server-backed, not same-origin: zero-weight gate gates/constraints/judge.toml hro_gate_shared requires a UI-created job and candidate to be found by the Observer in 'a new independent empty browser context' and states 'a browser-only save ... does not satisfy the gate'; the same check is repeated as the global gate in functional/prompt.md:11 ('A reload or a second tab of the same context is not independent'). hro_reorder, hro_add_candidate and hro_job_open require another person's independent context to see the same order/records; hro_stale_refused and hro_undo_conflict need cross-session server state. (3) Re-auth: hro_reorder reads order as Mei Lin after a fresh sign-in (rules:59 'Order survives a reload, a fresh sign-in and a restart'); drafts, which the brief deliberately makes browser/person-scoped ('Where drafts are kept is yours', rules:174-175), are graded across view changes and reload in hro_drafts and across ended session, re-sign-in and another user on the same browser in polish hro_pol_session_resume (w2.5) - matching instruction.md:7 'when I sign back in it is still there, and nobody else who signs in on that browser sees it' and rules:105-106 for note drafts. (4) Restart: hro_restart (w1.5) requires the seeded order/note read in Z, then after restart_app and fresh sign-in that jobs, per-stage order, notes, messages and activity are unchanged and starting data not reloaded; restart_mcp.py relaunches node on the same DB_PATH (test.sh:127-193), byte-identical to the template; only the functional dimension wires the single-use verifier MCP, so the marker cannot be consumed elsewhere. This matches instruction.md:13-15 (durable data in /app/app.db, keep new work across restarts) and integration.md. Counterexample probes: an in-memory Express app passes the gate and most rows but loses hro_restart; a reseed-on-boot app loses hro_restart (seeded order/note and 'not loaded again'); a localStorage-only board fails the independent-context gate and zeroes every binary row; a conforming app keeping drafts server-side per user still passes hro_drafts/hro_pol_session_resume because storage location is not prescribed. No hidden durability requirement found. Measured evidence: scripted golden run (workspace.json, hash verified, frozen solution hashes match) reports 'restart keeps jobs, cards, order, messages and activity without reseeding; live updates resume': passed, and 'session ended mid-draft ... another person sees no draft': passed. Risk=true because no full configured functional judge run exists (raw-evidence-index scope: 'Full configured grading/workload ... absent'): hro_restart is protocol D, the last step of a very long 9000 s functional protocol, and the prompt maps budget exhaustion to 'NOT EXERCISED' binary 0, so whether a conforming app's durability is actually observed within budget is unmeasured. This is a workload/evidence gap, not a demonstrated coverage defect for this row.
